description.fr-FR: L’enseignement du P. Louis Lallemant (1588-1635), maître des tertiaires jésuites et de toute une génération de spirituels (Surin, Rigoleuc, Saint-Jure), qui n’a rien écrit lui-même : ses disciples ont recueilli ses leçons, et le P. Pierre Champion les a ordonnées en sept principes (la vue de la fin, l’idée de la perfection, la pureté du cœur, la docilité à l’Esprit Saint, le recueillement et la vie intérieure, l’union avec Notre-Seigneur, l’ordre et les degrés de la vie spirituelle), publiées en 1694 avec sa Vie du P. Lallemant. Texte de la nouvelle édition de 1908 (Lecoffre-Gabalda), avec l’Addition de pensées recueillies par Surin.
description.en-US: The teaching of Father Louis Lallemant (1588-1635), instructor of the Jesuit tertians and of a whole generation of spiritual writers (Surin, Rigoleuc, Saint-Jure), who wrote nothing himself: his disciples noted down his lessons, and Father Pierre Champion arranged them in seven principles (the consideration of the end, the idea of perfection, purity of heart, docility to the Holy Spirit, recollection and the interior life, union with our Lord, the order and steps of the spiritual life) and published them in 1694 with his Life of Father Lallemant. The French is the 1908 new edition (Lecoffre-Gabalda), with the Additions of thoughts gathered by Surin; the English is the 1855 translation edited by F. W. Faber, which follows the same divisions chapter for chapter.
description.pt-BR: O ensinamento do Pe. Louis Lallemant (1588-1635), mestre dos terceiros-probantes jesuítas e de toda uma geração de espirituais (Surin, Rigoleuc, Saint-Jure), que nada escreveu: seus discípulos recolheram as lições, e o Pe. Pierre Champion as ordenou em sete princípios (a consideração do fim, a ideia da perfeição, a pureza de coração, a docilidade ao Espírito Santo, o recolhimento e a vida interior, a união com Nosso Senhor, a ordem e os graus da vida espiritual) e as publicou em 1694 com a Vida do Pe. Lallemant.

fr-FR.editor: P. Pierre Champion, S.J. (nouvelle édition, Paris: Lecoffre / Gabalda)

sources.edition: La Doctrine spirituelle du P. Louis Lallemant, de la Compagnie de Jésus, précédée de sa vie, nouvelle édition, Paris: Librairie Victor Lecoffre, J. Gabalda & Cie (Penn State copy, Google scan). Internet Archive OCR text.
sources.description: Champion's Avertissement and Vie du P. Lallemant, the seven principles with every section, chapter and article, and the Addition (pensées recueillies par le P. Surin, chapters I-X). Running heads, page numbers, § marks and line-end hyphens were stripped; the paragraph numbers (§) are dropped. The OCR was corrected with a French spelling dictionary and hand-made fixes for several hundred misreadings, so some OCR slips remain, mostly in Latin quotations and fused or split words. Article titles are kept as the first line of each article where the edition prints one. The table of contents and the Table des matières are not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Lallemant died in 1635; the text was compiled by Champion (d. 1701) and published in 1694; the 19th and early 20th century edition is public domain.

sources.edition: The Spiritual Doctrine of Father Louis Lallemant, of the Company of Jesus, preceded by some account of his life, translated from the French (Lecoffre 1846), edited by Frederick William Faber, London: Burns & Lambert, 1855. Oxford copy, Google scan, OCR text; the Advertisement and the Life are taken from the Sadlier reprint (New York, c. 1885; archive.org fatherlouislalle00lalluoft) because the Faber scan lacks its first pages.
sources.description: Chapters, articles and additions as in the French, same ids. The English OCR was cleaned of running heads and corrected only for the commonest misreadings, so more OCR slips remain than in the French. Faber's front matter is not imported.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in 1855 (London) and reprinted c. 1885: public domain. Translator anonymous; Faber died in 1863.
